title: Prove one lower-only phase cannot change an upper-shear endpoint (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration. One lower-only phase in a rational shear superposition word can be replaced by its binary mixing, preserving every required upper-supported endpoint entry and the exact paid profile.

```text
X = L F B
L,B over the upper-shear algebra; F over the lower-shear algebra
P([u_A v_K u_B]) = [u_(A+B)]
P(X) = L epsilon(F) B
upper-supported required entry => deletion preserves that entry
```

The new label retraction is well-defined for singular K and arbitrary rational or dyadic coefficients. It eliminates a proposed single-phase nonabelian escape before further word search. No new kappa, supplier or complete multiplication theorem is claimed.

## Task and overlap

Card `bit-helper-contract`, scope changed from G20 helper construction to the explicit first open question of Sagar Thakrar's [PR2613](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2613). Base main is `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`, priority revision 8. [TASK.json](research/single-lower-phase-deletion/TASK.json) retains the full frozen card, changed scope and exact source pins.

The theorem is an algebraic deletion reduction, distinct from ywz65's #2671 and Nick Petalas's #6027 invariant-lattice filters. dcharb78's #3183 separately reports a finite width-two block-Borel screen; its result is neither replayed nor claimed here. Exact main READMEs and the source proof are provenance pins, with no predecessor executable dependency.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19246973). The delivered factorization condition clarifies the claim's initial contiguity wording, as recorded in the [scope update](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19247260).

## Evidence

Before, the source handoff proposed one lower-left insertion without this deletion reduction. After, PROOF.md constructs an upper-shear bimodule retraction and proves deletion for every width and finite register count in the stated factorization class.

Local CPython 3.12.15, Darwin arm64, standard library only:

- Normal and optimized direct checks print `PASS_SINGLE_LOWER_PHASE_DELETION`. Each checks 4,256 complete finite-field triples, including 1,420 repeated-label comparisons; 144 rational triples, including 92 singular K; 144 bimodule identities; 24 full formal factorizations with 112 entries, including 42 upper-supported entries; six hypothesis/mutation controls and three dimension rejections.
- Both registered commands pass, with each direct command below one second locally against a 60-second limit. The final complete registered replay took 0.66 seconds. These timings establish replay budget only, not a performance improvement.
- Metadata and provenance checks pass. `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` authenticates all six package files and source ancestry to the pinned base.
- Official committed export and declared-input coverage pass. A fresh optimized Git-free replay with empty PATH and read-only exported files passes, preserving all seven exported files, including the export manifest. Receipts are generated and bound to package hashes.
- The selected binding-only orientation prints `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`; it was not a scientific selected replay.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/single-lower-phase-deletion/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/single-lower-phase-deletion/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/single-lower-phase-deletion
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/single-lower-phase-deletion --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 executable may replace the displayed path. The universal theorem follows from the written proof, not finite extrapolation.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The final product must have the factorization L F B. Ordinary one-sided circuits with a contiguous lower-only phase qualify. Chronological contiguity in a model permitting both left and right actions does not suffice by itself. Internal register-dependent Levi maps, separated lower phases and non-upper required entries are excluded. Clean auxiliary garbage is allowed; dirty-input independence requires including the relevant data-from-auxiliary zero entries among the preserved entries.

No general full-Borel impossibility or new three-call census is claimed. Physical legality, native operators, ownership/restoration beyond the declared entries, stock, precision/tape, uniform compiler, complete signed invoice and outer admission remain separate. No selected scientific replay, native replay, Lean, Docker or complete multiplier ran. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Credit

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Sagar Thakrar's PR2613 for the question and model, eumemic's PR288 for the register framework and existing upper-only obstruction, Swapnil Jain's related rank framework, ywz65's distinct gauge work, and the retained BIT lineage. General literature priority for elementary block multiplication and bimodule methods is unclaimed. Apache-2.0; predecessor notices remain unchanged.

## Open next questions

- Can separated lower phases yield a favorable completed word? Start with a width-two word, exact data endpoint and full paid/target invoice. No such saving or physical caller is supplied here.
- What deletion criterion survives internal Levi maps? First specify the enlarged middle alphabet and test its label collisions. The supplied Levi identity already rejects naive deletion.

## Related open work

Completion refresh inspected the titles and stated scopes of all 14 other open account PRs created since the advance CLAIM, #6149 through #6163 excluding this PR. None studies rational upper/lower single-phase deletion or supplies a competing value. No additional mathematical replays or comparisons were run.

No other open PR found in the live overlap corpus studies this exact single-lower-phase deletion question. Adjacent rational formal-register work has different endpoint/alphabet contracts:

- #6079 proves a minimum for one added scaled rank-one frame; this contribution changes the lower-update phase contract and computes no competing minimum.
- #6089 classifies positive extra-frame use and attainable lengths; this contribution supplies a deletion map, without a positive-frame classification or length spectrum.
- #6111 excludes two added positive frames at seven calls; this contribution does not evaluate those profiles or claim their floor.
- #6148 excludes one half-frame candidate by two-use lattice descent; this contribution requires no such lattice descent and computes no candidate call count.

No extra computations were run to compare predecessor numbers. The complete open-PR/Discussion overlap snapshot, targeted merged searches and current-main text searches are coordination evidence, not a novelty certificate; sparse local-note coverage remains incomplete.

## CI notes

Separately, completing planning would still fail on two documentation mismatches inherited unchanged from main `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`, whose PR6030 admission commit includes `[skip ci]`:

- `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record` expects `make frontier6030-verify` in `docs/ci.md`; the current section still describes #5599 and its replay command.

I read the comparison logs: [PR6150 run 40724809789](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40724809789) and [PR6120 run 40691776027](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40691776027) both finish with exactly those two failures. [Open PR6050](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6050) targets the documentation repair. This isolated package changes neither affected documentation nor their tests.

All local checks listed above passed, but they are not hosted certification. A maintainer must re-run CI after main is fixed, with planning able to finish within its time budget. No code was pushed, no CI re-run was requested, and main's docs were not changed for this completion.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: package.

Only six new files under `research/single-lower-phase-deletion/`, with opt-in replay. Shared code, frozen inputs and the selected frontier are unchanged.
